exposure: mode of first delivery (spontaneous vaginal delivery, assisted vaginal delivery, unplanned cesarean section, elective cesarean section)
cohort: The study included 375,619 women in Finland who had their first delivery between 2004 and 2016 and subsequently had a second pregnancy leading to birth by 2018.
finding: Women who had an assisted vaginal delivery or an unplanned cesarean section had higher subsequent birth rates, while those who had an elective cesarean section had lower subsequent birth rates, compared to women with spontaneous vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Women with assisted vaginal delivery (aHR, 1.23) and unplanned cesarean section (aHR, 1.03) had higher subsequent birth rates, whereas women with elective cesarean section (aHR, 0.86) had lower birth rates, compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery.
followup_time: Individual follow-up from the first delivery (between 2004 and 2016) until a second pregnancy or the end of the study period (2018), with a maximum follow-up of up to 14 years.
